title: "Writing a model in R"

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
has_highs <- requireNamespace("highs", quietly = TRUE)
```

```{r setup}
library(multimod)
```

multimod models are usually read from a source file: `read_gams()` and
`read_gmpl()` turn a GAMS or MathProg model into the structure described here.
This article builds the same kind of object directly in R, which is the way
to write a new model, to generate one programmatically, or to understand what
the readers produce. The model is a small capacity-expansion problem: three
technologies supply electricity to two regions at least cost. It ships with
the package as `example_models$toy`; the code below reproduces it.

## The parts of a model

A model is a list of named components, each a small S3 object:

| Component   | Constructor       | Holds                                              |
|-------------|-------------------|----------------------------------------------------|
| sets        | `new_set()`       | the index values of a dimension                    |
| mappings    | `new_mapping()`   | tuples over several sets, used as domains          |
| parameters  | `new_parameter()` | data indexed by dimensions                         |
| variables   | `new_variable()`  | decision variables, with a domain and bounds       |
| equations   | `new_equation()`  | left side, relation, right side, over a domain     |

The sides of an equation are *expressions*: trees of nodes of the abstract
syntax tree (AST), built with
`ast_variable()`, `ast_parameter()`, `ast_expression()`, `ast_sum()` and
their relatives. Every renderer (`as_gams()`, `as_latex()`, the LP matrix) is
a walk over that tree.

## Sets

A set names a dimension and lists its values.

```{r sets}
techs   <- c("coal", "gas", "wind")
regions <- c("north", "south")

sets <- list(
  tech   = new_set("tech",   desc = "generation technologies", data = techs),
  region = new_set("region", desc = "model regions",           data = regions)
)
sets$tech
```

## Mappings

A mapping is a table of tuples over one or more sets. Mappings serve as
*domains*: an indexed variable or equation exists for exactly the tuples of
its domain mapping, which is how sparse models stay sparse. Here every
technology may be built in every region, so the domain is the full grid.

```{r mappings}
tuples <- expand.grid(tech = techs, region = regions, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

mappings <- list(
  mTR = new_mapping("mTR", desc = "technology x region pairs",
                    dims = c("tech", "region"), data = tuples),
  mR  = new_mapping("mR",  desc = "regions",
                    dims = "region", data = data.frame(region = regions))
)
mappings$mTR$data
```

## Parameters

A parameter declares its dimensions and carries a data frame with one column
per dimension plus `value`.

```{r parameters}
parameters <- list(
  pCapCost = new_parameter("pCapCost", desc = "annualized capacity cost, EUR/kW",
    dims = "tech",
    data = data.frame(tech = techs, value = c(120, 70, 90))),
  pVarCost = new_parameter("pVarCost", desc = "variable cost, EUR/MWh",
    dims = "tech",
    data = data.frame(tech = techs, value = c(30, 55, 0))),
  pAvail = new_parameter("pAvail", desc = "availability factor",
    dims = c("tech", "region"),
    data = transform(tuples, value = c(0.85, 0.85, 0.90, 0.90, 0.35, 0.25))),
  pDemand = new_parameter("pDemand", desc = "annual demand, MWh",
    dims = "region",
    data = data.frame(region = regions, value = c(1000, 600)))
)
parameters$pAvail
```

## Variables

Variables declare dimensions, a domain mapping, a type and bounds. A scalar
variable has `dims = character(0)`.

```{r variables}
variables <- list(
  vCap = new_variable("vCap", desc = "installed capacity, kW",
                      dims = c("tech", "region"), domain = "mTR",
                      vtype = "positive", bounds = list(lo = 0)),
  vGen = new_variable("vGen", desc = "generation, MWh",
                      dims = c("tech", "region"), domain = "mTR",
                      vtype = "positive", bounds = list(lo = 0)),
  vCost = new_variable("vCost", desc = "total system cost, EUR",
                       dims = character(0))
)
```

## Expressions

Inside an equation, symbols are *referenced* rather than declared:
`ast_variable()` and `ast_parameter()` take the name and the index symbols,
given as `ast_dims()`. `ast_expression()` combines two nodes with an operator,
and `ast_sum()` sums an expression over index symbols.

```{r expressions}
gen   <- ast_variable("vGen", dims = ast_dims("tech", "region"))
avail <- ast_parameter("pAvail", dims = ast_dims("tech", "region"))
cap   <- ast_variable("vCap", dims = ast_dims("tech", "region"))

limit <- ast_expression("*", avail, cap)
node_type(limit)
limit
```

Rendering is a method on the node, so an expression can be checked before it
is used:

```{r render-expression}
as_gams(limit)
as_latex(limit)
```

## Equations

An equation has a left side, a relation (`"=="`, `"<="`, `">="`), a right side
and a domain. The domain mapping decides for which tuples the equation is
generated.

```{r equations}
eqCapLim <- new_equation("eqCapLim", desc = "generation is limited by capacity",
  dims = c("tech", "region"),
  lhs = gen, rhs = limit, relation = "<=",
  domain = ast_mapping("mTR", dims = ast_dims("tech", "region")))

eqDemand <- new_equation("eqDemand", desc = "demand is met in every region",
  dims = "region",
  lhs = ast_sum(ast_dims("tech"), ast_variable("vGen", dims = ast_dims("tech", "region"))),
  rhs = ast_parameter("pDemand", dims = ast_dims("region")),
  relation = ">=",
  domain = ast_mapping("mR", dims = ast_dims("region")))

eqCost <- new_equation("eqCost", desc = "total cost",
  dims = character(0),
  lhs = ast_variable("vCost", dims = ast_dims()),
  rhs = ast_sum(ast_dims("tech", "region"),
    ast_expression("+",
      ast_expression("*", ast_parameter("pCapCost", dims = ast_dims("tech")),
                          ast_variable("vCap", dims = ast_dims("tech", "region"))),
      ast_expression("*", ast_parameter("pVarCost", dims = ast_dims("tech")),
                          ast_variable("vGen", dims = ast_dims("tech", "region"))))),
  relation = "==")

eqDemand
as_latex(eqCost)
```

## The model

`new_model()` assembles the components. The objective is declared as the
equation that defines it, the variable it defines and the sense.

```{r model}
toy <- new_model(
  name = "toy", desc = "two-region capacity expansion toy model",
  sets = sets, mappings = mappings, parameters = parameters,
  variables = variables,
  equations = list(eqCapLim = eqCapLim, eqDemand = eqDemand, eqCost = eqCost),
  objectives = list(list(equation = "eqCost", variable = "vCost",
                         sense = "minimize"))
)
toy
```

Every constructor validates its node against the AST schema as it is built
(`ast_schema()` lists the node types and their fields), so a malformed node is
refused where it is written. `validate()` checks the assembled model: every
symbol referenced in an equation must be declared, with matching dimensions.

```{r validate}
v <- validate(toy)
v$valid
```

The code generators write indexed expressions with short iterator names
(`sum{t in tech}` in MathProg, `for t in tech` in Julia). A model built in R
has none until `add_index_aliases()` derives them from the set names:

```{r aliases}
toy <- add_index_aliases(toy)
unlist(toy$index_aliases)
```

## Solving

The matrix route needs no external software: `model_to_lp()` builds the
constraint matrix from the equations and the data, and `solve_highs()` passes
it to the HiGHS solver (the 'highs' package).

```{r lp}
lp <- model_to_lp(toy)
dim(lp$A)
```

```{r solve, eval = has_highs}
r <- solve_highs(toy, attach = FALSE)
r$objective
head(r$primal[r$primal$value > 0, ], 10)
```

The code-generation routes render the same model for an external solver:
`write_gmpl()` for GLPK, `write_jump()` for JuMP and `write_pyomo()` for
Pyomo; the [Solving and reading results](solving.html) article runs each with
its `solve_*()` counterpart.

```{r write}
mod_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".mod")
write_gmpl(toy, file = mod_file)
cat(head(readLines(mod_file), 12), sep = "\n")
```

## Saving and exchanging the model

`model_to_json()` serializes the whole model, including the AST, in the
language-neutral JSON format defined by `ast_json_schema()`;
`model_from_json()` reads it back. This is the interchange format for other
implementations of the model structure.

```{r json}
json <- model_to_json(toy)
back <- model_from_json(json)
identical(names(back$equations), names(toy$equations))
as_gams(back$equations$eqDemand)
```

`save_model()` and `load_model()` write a model as a workspace directory with
its data tables in CSV or Arrow files; see the
[Model workspace and data](model_workspace.html) article.
